AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 19, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Margarita L. Rios, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
  Luigi Vernola, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8082-013-905; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Department of the Air Force; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  III.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR -
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez; regarding negotiations with the Norwalk
  Association of Management Employees.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Eddie Cuen
  Trinity Lutheran Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Aremi Rodriguez, 5th grade
  Edmondson Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize John Glenn High School Wrestling Team for Winning CIF Division 6 Duals.

  II.  The City Council to recognize March as National Social Service Worker Month.

  III.  City Council to recognize Public Safety and Social Service staff, as well as Los Angeles County
  Department of Mental Health staff for exemplary service in assisting a community member
  experiencing homelessness.

  IV.  City Council to recognize the Public Safety Department on its 30th Anniversary.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  2020 Census, Norwalk Campaign Efforts

  2.  Youth Baseball League Opening Day

  3.  Project No. 7196 – Status Update and Concept Plan for Design of Firestone Boulevard widening from
   Hoxie Avenue to Imperial Highway

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of March 5,
  2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period February 10, 2019 –
  February 23, 2019, in the total amount of $907,793.63. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  February 27, 2019 - March 12, 2019, in the total amount of $1,162,269.04. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Hilda and
  Demetria Alvarez, Shannon Clark, and Frank Romero. 830-01/03/18

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – MARCH 13, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-10 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 19-10, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE HUMAN
  RESOURCES AND TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENTS.

  Report

  7.  PROJECT NO. 7440 – ALONDRA BOULEVARD, PIONEER BOULEVARD, AND 160TH STREET
  WATER MAIN INSTALLATION PROJECT - APPROVAL OF PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS AND
  AUTHORIZATION FOR ADVERTISEMENT TO BID – Staff recommends City Council approve the
  plans and specifications for the construction of the Alondra Boulevard, Pioneer Boulevard, and 160th
  Street water main installation project, authorize the advertisement of bids, and set a bid opening date
  of April 24, 2019. 1005-04-7440

  Report

  8.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-06 - CALIFORNIA LOW CARBON TRANSIT OPERATIONS PROGRAM
  (LCTOP) FISCAL YEAR 2018-19 ALLOCATION REQUEST - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 19-06, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTION OF THE LOW CARBON TRANSIT OPERATIONS PROGRAM
  (LCTOP) PROJECT, in the amount of $117,304. 1105-02

  Report

  9.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENTS TO CITYWIDE LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT – Staff
  recommends City Council authorize the City Manager to execute amendments to the agreement with
  Priority Landscape Services, LLC, on behalf of the City, provided there is funding in the budget, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 945

  Report
   10. AGREEMENT - DOCUMENT SCANNING SERVICES – Staff recommends City Council approve an
  agreement with Konica Minolta Business Solutions U.S.A. to provide document scanning services in an
  amount not to exceed $179,574 from the effective date of the agreement until the services are
  completed; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided
  there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 870-11

  Report

  11. REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR CARNIVAL – DATE CHANGE – Staff
  recommends City Council approve the change of date request by the Norwalk Float Foundation for the
  dates of March 26 through April 1, 2019. 920-01-02

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  12. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  13. ACCEPT WORK – FISCAL YEAR 2018/19 CROSSWALK STRIPING – Staff recommends City Council
  accept the work of Superior Pavement Markings, Inc. in the amount of $21,356.60 for the installation of
  thermoplastic crosswalk lines at eight (8) school sites. 1050-03-01

  Report

  14. APPROVAL OF AN EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATING AGREEMENT FOR THE TANK FARM PROPERTY –
  Staff recommends City Council approve an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement with Lewis Acquisition
  Company, LLC (Lewis Management Corp.) to assist the City in tasks required for the development of
  Tank Farm property; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments
  provided there is funding in budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 935-
  01

  Report

  15. THE 2018 NORWALK GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT –
  Staff recommends City Council receive and file the 2018 General Plan and Housing Element Annual
  Progress Report, and direct staff to forward a copy of the report to the Governor’s Office of Planning
  and Research and to the State Department of Housing and Community Development prior to April 1,
  2019. 320-02

  Report

  16. PROPOSED ACTIVITIES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR THE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS
  PROGRAM – City Council direction is requested concerning the proposed CDBG and HOME activities
  for the draft FY 2019/20 Annual Action Plan. 315-01-05

  Report

  17. RESOLUTION NO. 19-09 – ENGAGEMENT OF FINANCIAL ADVISORS, BOND COUNSEL, AND
  UNDERWRITERS FOR THE PROPOSED ISSUANCE OF BONDS FOR STREET AND WATER
  IMPROVEMENTS - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-09, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE ENGAGEMENT OF
  MUNICIPAL ADVISORS AND BOND COUNSEL FOR THE PROPOSED ISSUANCE OF BONDS FOR
  STREET AND WATER SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS, THE SELECTION OF UNDERWRITERS FOR
  THE SALE OF SUCH BONDS, AND TAKING CERTAIN RELATED ACTIONS.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
 ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated March 15, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
